q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm, AE = 4 cm. Find EC.
q.e: A line parallel to one side cuts the other two in the same ratio (BPT): 2/3 = 4/EC, so EC = 6.

q.t: Which triangles are ALWAYS similar to each other?
q.e: Every equilateral triangle has angles 60°, 60°, 60°, so any two match by AA.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 4 cm, PQ = 8 cm and BC = 5 cm. Find QR.
q.e: Corresponding sides are in one ratio: PQ/AB = 2, so QR = 2 × 5.

q.t: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar by…
q.e: Two equal angles force the third to be equal too (sum 180°), so the shape is fixed.

q.t: The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles equals the ratio of their…
q.e: Each side is scaled by the same factor, so their sum (the perimeter) is scaled by that factor too.

q.t: Are all circles similar?
o: Yes — any circle is a scaled copy of any other
No — only circles of equal radius
Only circles with the same centre
q.e: Similar means same shape, maybe different size. Every circle has the same shape; enlarge or shrink one and it fits exactly on another.

q.t: Two polygons with the same number of sides are similar if their corresponding angles are equal AND…
o: their corresponding sides are in the same ratio
one pair of sides is equal
q.e: Both conditions are needed: same angles keep the shape, and one common ratio for all sides means a true scaling.

q.t: Is a square similar to a rhombus that is not a square?
o: No — their angles are not equal
Yes — all sides are in the same ratio
Only when the sides are equal
q.e: The side ratios do match (all sides equal in both), but the rhombus has angles other than 90°. Equal ratios alone are not enough for polygons.

q.t: The Basic Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle, cutting the other two sides, divides those sides…
q.e: The parallel line cuts off a smaller triangle with the same angles, so it is a scaled copy — the cuts on the two sides are in the same ratio.

q.t: In ΔABC, D is on AB and E on AC with AD/DB = AE/EC. What can you say about DE?
q.e: This is the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem: if a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC. AD/DB = 3/5 and AC = 5.6 cm. Find AE.
q.e: AD/DB = 3/5 means AE is 3 of 8 equal parts of AC: 3/8 × 5.6.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = x, DB = x − 3, AE = x + 3 and EC = x − 2. Find x.
q.e: BPT: x/(x − 3) = (x + 3)/(x − 2). Cross-multiply: x² − 2x = x² − 9, so x = 4.5.

q.t: A 6 m pole casts a 4 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 28 m shadow. How tall is the tower?
q.e: Sun rays make the same angle, so the triangles are similar: height/shadow = 6/4, so 28 × 1.5.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm and EC = 4 cm. Find AE.
q.e: By BPT, AD/DB = AE/EC, so 1.5/3 = AE/4 and AE = 4 × 0.5 = 2.

q.t: D and E are on sides PQ and PR of ΔPQR with PD = 4, DQ = 4.5, PE = 8 and ER = 9 cm. Is DE ∥ QR?
o: You cannot tell without the angles
q.e: 4/4.5 = 8/9 and 8/9 = 8/9. The two sides are cut in the same ratio, so by the converse of BPT, DE ∥ QR.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with ∠A = 47° and ∠E = 83°. Find ∠C in degrees.
q.e: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles: ∠B = ∠E = 83°. Then ∠C = 180° − 47° − 83° = 50°.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB = 3, BC = 4, CA = 5 cm and PQ = 6 cm. Find the perimeter of ΔPQR.
q.e: PQ/AB = 6/3 = 2, so every side of ΔPQR is twice as long: 6, 8, 10. Perimeter 24 cm.

q.t: One triangle has sides 4, 6, 8 cm and another 6, 9, 12 cm. Are they similar?
o: Yes, by SSS — every ratio is 2 : 3
q.e: Match smallest with smallest: 4/6 = 6/9 = 8/12 = 2/3. All three sides in one ratio means the triangles are similar (SSS).

q.t: In ΔABC, D is the midpoint of AB and DE ∥ BC meets AC at E. AC = 9 cm. Find AE.
q.e: By BPT, AE/EC = AD/DB = 1, so E is the midpoint of AC: AE = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔQRP. Which angle equals ∠B?
q.e: The order of letters gives the matching: A ↔ Q, B ↔ R, C ↔ P. So ∠B = ∠R.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at A and AD ⊥ BC. BD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. Find AD.
q.e: The altitude to the hypotenuse makes two similar triangles, giving AD² = BD × DC = 36.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at A and AD ⊥ BC with BD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm. Find AB.
q.e: ΔABD ~ ΔCBA gives AB² = BD × BC = 4 × 13 = 52, so AB = 2√13.

q.t: A girl 1.5 m tall walks away from the foot of a 4.5 m lamp-post at 1.2 m/s. How long is her shadow after 5 seconds?
q.e: She is 6 m from the post. Similar triangles: 1.5/s = 4.5/(6 + s), so 4.5s = 9 + 1.5s and s = 3.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = x, DB = x − 2, AE = x + 2 and EC = x − 1. Find x.
q.e: BPT: x/(x − 2) = (x + 2)/(x − 1). Cross-multiply: x² − x = x² − 4, so x = 4.

q.t: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC; its diagonals meet at O. AO = 6, OC = 4 and BO = 9 cm. Find OD.
q.e: AB ∥ DC makes ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD (alternate angles are equal, AA). So AO/OC = BO/OD: 6/4 = 9/OD, OD = 6.

q.t: In ΔPQR, ST ∥ QR with S on PQ and T on PR. PS = 2 cm, SQ = 6 cm and QR = 12 cm. Find ST.
q.e: ST ∥ QR gives ΔPST ~ ΔPQR (AA). Use the whole side PQ = 8, not SQ: ST/QR = PS/PQ = 2/8, so ST = 3.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with BC = 6 cm and EF = 9 cm. The altitude from A is 4 cm. Find the altitude from D.
q.e: Each altitude makes a right triangle with ∠B (or ∠E), and ∠B = ∠E, so those right triangles are similar (AA). So altitudes are in the ratio of sides, 6 : 9 — the altitude is 4 × 9/6 = 6.

q.t: In ΔABC, P is on AB and Q on AC with AP = 3, PB = 6, AQ = 4 and QC = 8 cm. BC = 15 cm. Find PQ.
q.e: AP/AB = 3/9 = 1/3 and AQ/AC = 4/12 = 1/3, with ∠A shared, so ΔAPQ ~ ΔABC (SAS). PQ = BC/3 = 5.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔFEG. CD and GH bisect ∠C and ∠G (D on AB, H on FE). AC = 8 cm, FG = 6 cm and CD = 4 cm. Find GH.
q.e: ∠A = ∠F, and the half-angles ∠ACD = ∠FGH, so ΔACD ~ ΔFGH (AA). CD/GH = AC/FG = 8/6, so GH = 3.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at C, and CD ⊥ AB. Which is true?
q.e: ΔADC and ΔCDB both have a right angle at D, and ∠A = ∠DCB (each is 90° minus ∠B), so they are similar. Then AD/CD = CD/DB, i.e. CD² = AD × DB.

q.t: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and the diagonals meet at O. AO = 3x − 1, OC = 5x − 3, BO = 2x + 1, OD = 6x − 5. Find x.
q.e: Parallel sides make AO/OC = BO/OD. Cross-multiplying gives 2x² − 5x + 2 = 0, so x = 2 or 1/2; x = 1/2 makes OC negative.

q.t: A boy 1.6 m tall stands 6 m from a lamp-post. His shadow is 2 m long. How tall is the lamp-post?
q.e: The boy and the post both stand straight up, so the boy-and-shadow triangle is similar to the post-and-whole-shadow triangle. h/(6 + 2) = 1.6/2, so h = 6.4.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD : DB = 3 : 2 and BC = 10 cm. Find DE.
q.e: ΔADE ~ ΔABC. The ratio to use is AD : AB = 3 : 5 (the whole side), so DE = 10 × 3/5 = 6.

q.t: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, AB = 12 cm and DC = 8 cm. Its diagonals meet at O and AC = 15 cm. Find AO.
q.e: ΔAOB ~ ΔCOD with ratio AB : CD = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2. So AO : OC = 3 : 2, and AO = 15 × 3/5 = 9.

q.t: In ΔABC, D is on AB and E on AC with AD = 2, AB = 6, AE = 3 and AC = 9 cm. BC = 12 cm. What is DE, and is DE ∥ BC?
o: DE = 4 cm, but DE is not parallel to BC
q.e: AD/AB = AE/AC = 1/3 with ∠A shared, so ΔADE ~ ΔABC (SAS) and DE = 12/3 = 4. Equal angles ∠ADE = ∠ABC are corresponding angles, so DE ∥ BC.

q.t: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR with AB/PQ = 2/3. AD and PM are medians, and AD = 8 cm. Find PM.
q.e: BD = BC/2 and QM = QR/2, so AB/PQ = BD/QM, and ∠B = ∠Q. So ΔABD ~ ΔPQM (SAS) and AD/PM = 2/3: PM = 12.

q.t: A mirror lies on the ground 6 m from a tree. A man whose eyes are 1.5 m high stands 2 m from the mirror, on the other side, and sees the top of the tree in it. How tall is the tree?
q.e: Light reflects at equal angles, so the man's triangle and the tree's triangle have equal angles at the mirror and right angles at the ground: they are similar. h/6 = 1.5/2, so h = 4.5.

q.t: In ΔABC, AD ⊥ BC with D between B and C, and AD² = BD × DC. Find ∠BAC in degrees.
q.e: AD/BD = DC/AD with right angles at D, so ΔADB ~ ΔCDA (SAS) and ∠BAD = ∠ACD. Then ∠BAC = ∠BAD + ∠DAC = ∠ACD + ∠DAC = 90°, the two acute angles of right ΔADC.

q.t: E is on side AD extended beyond D of parallelogram ABCD, and BE cuts CD at F. AB = 9, AD = 8 and AE = 12 cm. Find DF.
q.e: DF lies along DC, which is parallel to AB, so ΔEDF ~ ΔEAB (AA). DE = 12 − 8 = 4, so DF/AB = DE/AE = 4/12, DF = 3.

q.t: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 4x − 3, BD = 3x − 1, AE = 8x − 7 and CE = 5x − 3. Find x.
q.e: BPT: (4x − 3)/(3x − 1) = (8x − 7)/(5x − 3). Cross-multiply: 20x² − 27x + 9 = 24x² − 29x + 7, so 2x² − x − 1 = 0 and x = 1 or −1/2. x = −1/2 makes AD negative, so x = 1.
